_comment: Card D2: the scripted induction model of research/configs/d2-induce-fixture.json, written by hand in the shape AWM's prompt asks for. It answers only the request the induction sends for the config's sessions at each seed. Workflows 1 to 3 become candidates; workflow 4 has one action and workflow 5 calls a tool no example called, so both are rejected, which shows the guards in the run's rows.

replies.reply:
Workflow 1: Inspect a source file before changing it
Use when: a task names a source file whose current contents decide the change.
<think>
Looking at {source-file}.
</think>
<action>
read({"path":"{source-file}"})
</action>

<think>
I read it once more to find the exact place to change.
</think>
<action>
read({"path":"{source-file}"})
</action>

Workflow 2: Edit a file and check the edit
Use when: a task changes one file and the change must be seen to have applied.
<think>
I make the change in {source-file}.
</think>
<action>
edit({"path":"{source-file}"})
</action>

<think>
I read {source-file} again to check that the edit applied, rather than retrying a shell edit.
</think>
<action>
read({"path":"{source-file}"})
</action>

Workflow 3: Run a command, then read what it points at
Use when: a task starts from a command's output, such as a failing test or a search.
<think>
I run {command} to see where to look.
</think>
<action>
bash({"command":"{command}"})
</action>

<think>
The output points at {source-file}; I read it.
</think>
<action>
read({"path":"{source-file}"})
</action>

Workflow 4: Finish the task
Use when: the change is in place.
<action>
read({"path":"{source-file}"})
</action>

Workflow 5: Write a new file from scratch
Use when: a task needs a new file.
<action>
write({"path":"{new-file}"})
</action>
<action>
read({"path":"{new-file}"})
</action>
